diagnostic_evidence.quote: As a benchmark, we use the square root of the $(M+1)$-st eigenvalue of the integration operator associated with the kernel $\kappa$ and the probability measure $\pi$, divided by $\|\vzerov\|_{\mathcal{H}}$.
For each algorithm iteration, we plot the highest and lowest $\MMD$ value across all 100 initializations.

issues.failure_explanation: The experiments establish comparisons with tested algorithms, not proximity to the globally optimal quantization. No applicable optimality certificate is supplied, and the eigenvalue benchmark is not generally a lower bound. For the unit-bandwidth Gaussian kernel and π=(δ_{−a}+δ_a)/2, a one-node rule at zero has squared MMD (1−exp(−a²))²/2, whereas λ₂=(1−exp(−2a²))/2. Their ratio tends to zero as a tends to zero. Thus the eigenvalue scale cannot certify the claimed near-optimality, even for an empirical target and the kernel used in the experiments.

failure_location.quote: In particular, both MSIP and the WFR ODE yield \textit{near-optimal} quantizations under MMD, even with extremely adversarial initializations.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace near-optimality claims by the supported claim of low observed MMD relative to the tested baselines and the stated benchmark.
issues.overall_effect: The optimality language in the contributions and numerical discussion is unsupported; the reported empirical comparisons can remain.
issues.title: The numerical benchmark does not establish near-optimality
issues.why_classification: This withdraws a substantive optimality interpretation, but preserves the experiments and their comparative conclusions without requiring new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Existence of a limit or satisfaction of the steady-state equations does not imply even local minimality. For κ(x,y)=exp(−(x−y)²/2), π=(δ_{−a}+δ_a)/2 with a>1, and M=1, initialize y=0 and w=v₀(0)=exp(−a²/2). Both ODE derivatives vanish, so the trajectory has a constant limit. Yet F₁''(0)=−(a²−1)exp(−a²)<0: its node is a strict local maximum of the optimally weighted objective.

It is a positive-definite Gaussian mixture with bounded gradient. Its shadow kernel off the diagonal is Σ2^(n/2) exp(−2^(2n)r²/2); assign diagonal value 1. issues.failure_explanation: The algebraic identity does not make the direction a descent direction unless M is positive definite. The stated shadow-kernel assumption requires only symmetry. For example, take the unit Gaussian κ, let barκ equal κ off the diagonal and −1 on the diagonal, and take π=δ₀ with M=1. This symmetric shadow satisfies the stated gradient factorization. At y>0, W and both kernel matrices are nonsingular, but M=−v₀(y)² and Ψ_MSIP(y)=2y. Every positive damped step moves to (1+η)y and increases F₁.
